Understand main points, gist and detail in spoken and written French on the four themes.
Infer meaning from complex spoken and written material, including online media.
Summarise information from spoken sources.
Translate unseen passages from French into English and from English into French.
Write critical, analytical French responses on key concepts, characterisation, technique and social and cultural setting.
Present viewpoints, build arguments, draw conclusions and evaluate in writing.
Discuss a sub-theme from a stimulus statement, giving ideas, examples and justified views.
Research an independent topic related to French-speaking culture and society using written sources.
Summarise sources, give a personal response and discuss findings fluently.
Interact naturally, ask questions that elicit opinions and take the lead in discussion.
Use gender, plurals, and definite, indefinite and partitive articles correctly.
Use adjective agreement, position, comparatives, superlatives, and demonstrative, indefinite, possessive and interrogative adjectives.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers and time and date expressions.
Form adverbs in -ment, comparatives and superlatives, interrogative adverbs, and quantifiers.
Use subject, object, disjunctive and reflexive pronouns with correct position and order.
Use relative, demonstrative, indefinite, possessive and interrogative pronouns, and y and en.
Conjugate regular, modal, irregular and reflexive verbs with agreement, il y a, tu/vous and impersonal verbs.
Use verbs with infinitives, perfect infinitive, negative and interrogative forms.
Use present, perfect, imperfect and future tenses.
Use conditional, future perfect, conditional perfect and pluperfect, and recognise the past historic.
Use the infinitive, present participle, past participle and aller or venir de plus infinitive.
Use the passive voice in all tenses.
Use the present and perfect subjunctive, and recognise the imperfect subjunctive.
Use simple and complex prepositions, and coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
Use negative particles, ne with negative subjects, questions, commands and inversion.
Use depuis and il y a for time, comparative constructions and indirect speech.
Use discourse markers and fillers.
Study two works: two literary texts, or one literary text and one film, from the prescribed list.
Choose literary texts from novels, plays and short stories such as L'Étranger, Le Tartuffe and Une si longue lettre.
